D. Goals and Objectives
The citizens of Randolph, after numerous meetings and in conjunction with their elected representatives of the Randolph Planning Study Board, established the following goals and objectives to be met in removing the deficiencies of their community:
General Community Objectives
1. The elimination of deterioration, blight, and blighting influences through rehabilitation and staged demolition. 
a. Rehabilitation  to improve existing housing and surroundings to create an attractive, livable, healthful, safe, and physically sound community environment.
b. Redevelopment  emphasis on the construction of dwelling units to provide maximum number of low and moderate income ownership and rental opportunities, with occupancy priorties for the residents of the community.
2. To prevent further blight, by coordinating the rehabilitation and redevelopment objectives, regulations and controls herein will be implemented in a manner that will guarantee the environmental goals of the community.
The group also formulated an extensive list of specific objectives for both the redevelopment and the rehabilitation areas. These goals concern not only the physical upgrading of Randolph but also include a set of ambitious social goals (See Appendix, Exhibit No. 1).
E. Process of Decision Making
The following sequence of events comprise a summary history to date of the landmarks in the development and processing of the Randolph Project plans:
1. In February, 1967, the Richmond City Council approved the filing of an application by the Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority with the Department of Housing and Urban Development for loans and grants to be used in rehabilitation and redevelopment of the Randolph Community.
